title: Simulation-Enabled Evaluation of Advanced BIPV Roof Materials for Reducing Solar Heat Gain and Cooling Demand in Tropical Buildings
content: Building-integrated photovoltaics (BIPV) offer opportunities to combine renewable en-ergy generation with building-envelope functions; however, semi-transparent BIPV roofs can introduce substantial solar heat gain in tropical buildings. This study presents a simulation-enabled framework for evaluating advanced solar-control material strategies for BIPV roofs, using a high-occupancy food-court building in Singapore as a case study. A digital building performance model was developed in Integrated Environmental So-lutions Virtual Environment (IESVE) to investigate the effects of alternative BIPV mate-rial configurations on solar heat gain, indoor air temperature, and cooling demand. The existing semi-transparent BIPV roof was established as the baseline, and eight alternative material configurations incorporating upconversion nanoparticles (UCNPs), glass beads, polymer films, and composite laminates were comparatively evaluated using experi-mentally derived optical properties. The baseline roof produced a peak solar gain of 25.44 kW, a peak indoor air temperature of 24.88 °C, and a maximum hourly cooling energy demand of 267.37 kWh under the simulated conditions. Among the investigated configurations, UCNP/nylon and UCNP/nylon-on-PET-film exhibited the strongest overall performance. The UCNP/nylon configuration reduced peak solar gain by ap-proximately 66%, lowered peak indoor air temperature by approximately 2.6 °C, and reduced peak chiller demand compared with the baseline. The results demonstrate how digital building-performance simulation can support the screening and optimisation of emerging envelope materials before physical deployment. The proposed approach pro-vides a practical pathway for integrating advanced material technologies with building simulation to improve the thermal and energy performance of BIPV-enabled built assets in hot-humid climates.
